name: P21 (P021)

track.title: Research use only
track.line: Not FDA approved; research labels not for humans

what.text: P021 (Peptide 021) is a small lab-made compound built from part of ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF), a protein that supports nerve cells. Its developers took a four-amino-acid piece from what they call the most active region of CNTF and added an adamantylated glycine to one end. They say this was done to help it cross the blood–brain barrier and to slow its breakdown in the body.

what.text: The developers describe P021 as a pentapeptide, Ac-DGGL(A)G-NH2, with a molecular weight of 578.3. Most of the work comes from one group, led by Khalid Iqbal at the New York State Institute for Basic Research in Developmental Disabilities.

what.text: A 2010 paper from the same group used the name “P21” for the compound Ac-DGGLAG-NH2. Later papers call it P021 or Peptide 021.

what.text: How it acts, according to animal and lab studies:

items.text: The authors describe P021 as a neurotrophic and neurogenic compound: in their mouse and rat studies it was linked to more new nerve cells in the hippocampus and to more markers of synapses (the contacts between nerve cells).

src.label: Baazaoui and Iqbal, Alzheimers Res Ther, 2017
Bolognin et al., Neurobiol Aging, 2014

items.text: In Alzheimer's model mice, the authors report higher brain levels of BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor) and lower activity of the enzyme GSK-3β with P021.

src.label: Kazim et al., Neurobiol Dis, 2014

items.text: In aged rats, the authors report that P021 crosses the blood–brain barrier.

src.label: Khatoon et al., J Alzheimers Dis, 2015

what.text: Two of the papers disclose that the group's senior author, Khalid Iqbal, holds US patents on CNTF-derived peptides such as P021. The 2026 paper adds that he co-founded a company that holds a worldwide license to develop P021 as a drug.

src.label: Kazim et al., Sci Rep, 2017
Falangola et al., Magn Reson Imaging, 2026

what.text: No study of P021 in people has been published. All of the evidence is in mice, rats and cells.

research.text: No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026. Every study below was done in mice, rats or cells, almost all by the group that developed P021.
A PubMed search returned 17 records; none was a study in people. A ClinicalTrials.gov search found no trial of this compound.

research.title: Starting early in Alzheimer's model mice, 2017

facts.v: Baazaoui N, Iqbal K. Alzheimers Res Ther 2017;9(1):45
P021 or a plain (vehicle) diet; normal mice as a comparison group
108 female mice: 32 3xTg-AD mice given P021, 35 3xTg-AD mice given vehicle, and 41 normal mice. 3xTg-AD mice have three human gene changes linked to Alzheimer's disease
from 3 months of age, before plaques or tangles appear, to 21 months of age
P021 mixed into the feed at 60 nmol per gram of food
new nerve cells, dendrite and synapse markers, Morris water maze (spatial memory) at 9 months of treatment and an object-location task at 15–16 months

research.found: The authors report that P021 prevented the loss of dendrite and synapse markers, increased new nerve cells, and reversed memory problems in the 3xTg-AD mice.

research.title: Plaques, tangles and survival in the same model, 2017

facts.v: Baazaoui N, Iqbal K. J Alzheimers Dis 2017;58(1):215-230
female 3xTg-AD mice, treatment started at 3 months of age
followed at 9, 15 and 18 months of treatment
nerve-cell loss, amyloid-β and tau changes, object-recognition memory and deaths

research.found: The authors report less nerve-cell loss, less amyloid-β and tau change, better object-recognition memory and fewer deaths with P021.

src.label: Baazaoui and Iqbal, J Alzheimers Dis, 2017

research.title: Older Alzheimer's model mice, 2014

facts.v: Kazim SF, et al. Neurobiol Dis 2014;71:110-30
female 3xTg-AD and normal mice, treatment started at 9–10 months of age
12 months of P021 or vehicle diet
tau changes, amyloid-β, BDNF, GSK-3β, memory, new nerve cells and synapse markers

research.found: Abnormal tau fell. The effect on amyloid-β was limited to lower soluble amyloid-β and a trend toward less plaque in one part of the hippocampus. The authors also report better memory and more new nerve cells.

src.label: Kazim et al., Neurobiol Dis, 2014

research.title: Aged rats, 2014

facts.v: Bolognin S, et al. Neurobiol Aging 2014;35(9):2134-46
Fisher rats aged 22 to 24 months
long-term P021 by mouth
learning and memory, new nerve cells, BDNF, synapse markers, and brain chemistry by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

research.found: The authors report less age-related decline in learning and memory, more new nerve cells, more BDNF and fewer synapse losses with P021.

src.label: Bolognin et al., Neurobiol Aging, 2014

research.title: Tau in the spinal fluid of aged rats, 2015

facts.v: Khatoon S, et al. J Alzheimers Dis 2015;47(3):557-64
aged Fisher rats
whether P021 enters the brain, tau and amyloid-β in brain and spinal fluid, and immune reaction

research.found: P021 crossed the blood–brain barrier. It lowered tau, but not amyloid-β, in spinal fluid, to levels seen in young rats. The authors found no detectable immune reaction in the rats.

facts.v: Li B, et al. FEBS Lett 2010;584(15):3359-65
normal adult C57Bl6 mice

research.found: The authors report that the compound, given outside the brain, improved learning and memory and increased new nerve cells in normal mice.

items.text: treatment from before birth to early life in Ts65Dn mice. The authors report less developmental delay in pups and better memory in adulthood.

items.text: 3xTg-AD and normal female mice were fed P021 from day 8 of pregnancy to day 21 after birth, then a normal diet. The authors report better memory at 4 months and less tau change and plaque at 22 months.

research.title: CDKL5 deficiency model, 2024

facts.v: Mottolese N, et al. J Neurodev Disord 2024;16(1):65
a human nerve-cell line lacking CDKL5, and young and adult Cdkl5 knockout mice
nerve-cell growth and survival in cells; BDNF, brain structure and behavior in mice

research.found: P021 helped the nerve cells in the dish. In the mice, long-term P021 did not raise BDNF or improve brain structure, and behavior improved only a little.

us.text: Not FDA approved for any use. No P021 product is in Drugs@FDA and no trial is registered. Products labelled “research use only” are not for human use. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA does not allow products labelled “for research use only” to be sold for people to take. In a 2020 consumer flyer about fake COVID-19 products, FDA said products marketed “for research use only,” or otherwise not for human consumption, “have not been evaluated for safety and should never be used by humans.” In a 2026 statement about GLP-1 drugs, FDA said it has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved drugs “falsely labeled ‘for research purposes’ or ‘not for human consumption’” to consumers for human use. Neither statement names P021; they are FDA's general statements about such labels.

after.text: P021 is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA’s class S0 bans at all times any pharmacological substance not covered elsewhere on the List and with no current approval by any government health regulator for human therapeutic use, including drugs still in development. For 2027, WADA adds “peptides” to the examples in S0. The lists do not say whether P021 falls under S0.
